cover.title: ANATOMY OF A VERDICT
cover.lead: Ruth Adair's husband fell down the iron stairs of their mill. Eleven jurors say she pushed him. You are juror twelve, and you are not sure.
cover.small: Single player · C1 · two forks, four endings
cover.object: the empty twelfth chair at the jury table
cover.picture: A long oak jury table in a tall Victorian room, eleven chairs filled with blurred figures on the left in shadow, and on the right one empty leather chair pulled back, lit by a brass desk lamp. Rain on the tall window behind.

briefing.title: HOW TO CONCEDE A POINT

cards.head: ALTHOUGH / EVEN THOUGH + CLAUSE
cards.text: Although she was angry, nobody saw her push him.

cards.head: DESPITE / IN SPITE OF + NOUN OR -ING
cards.text: Despite the shouting, the recording proves nothing.

cards.head: EVEN SO / STILL / AND YET
cards.text: She lied about the time. Even so, that isn't murder.

cards.head: ADJECTIVE + AS / THOUGH + CLAUSE
cards.text: Strange as it sounds, the rail was already loose.

cards.head: MAY ... BUT / MUCH AS + CLAUSE
cards.text: She may have been furious, but furious isn't guilty.

briefing.note: Concede the point first, then turn it. Never ALTHOUGH ... BUT in one sentence, and never DESPITE + a subject and verb.

choices.title: WHAT DO WE REOPEN?
choices.story: Gerald gives in. "One piece of evidence, then we vote again. Your choice." Two exhibits wait on the court trolley.
choices.object: the evidence trolley by the door
choices.picture: A wheeled metal court trolley by a panelled door, on it a closed laptop and a stack of large photographs tied with pink tape, lit by the lamp on the trolley's corner. Left half: the bare panelled wall.

routes.label: REPLAY THE RECORDING
routes.note: Your trade. Every second, every echo, every gap.

routes.label: STUDY THE STAIRWELL
routes.note: Priya's trade. The photographs, the rail, the fall.

choices.title: WHERE DOES THE DOUBT LIE?
choices.story: Victor folds his arms. "Give me one reason." You have two: the apprentice who heard them, or the doorbell camera across the lane.
choices.object: the two exhibit folders under the lamp
choices.picture: Two closed card folders side by side on the oak table, one buff and one blue, under a brass desk lamp, Victor's folded tweed arms just in frame behind them. Left half: dim table top and wall.

routes.label: QUESTION THE WITNESS
routes.note: Kit Marlow, nineteen, the apprentice. He says he heard a scream.

routes.label: RUN THE CLOCK
routes.note: A doorbell camera, a white van, a 999 call. Twenty-seven minutes.

endings.label: UNANIMOUS
endings.title: NOT GUILTY, TWELVE TO NONE
endings.text: Twelve slips, one word. Ruth Adair grips the rail of the dock and does not cry. You will never know what happened on those stairs. That was the point: nobody in that room could know.
endings.object: Ruth's hands on the brass rail of the dock
endings.picture: The glass-walled dock of an English courtroom, Ruth Adair standing in a dark suit, both hands gripping the polished brass rail, a shaft of pale light on her hands. Left half: empty wooden benches.

endings.label: VERDICT REACHED
endings.title: NOT GUILTY
endings.text: Eleven to one is enough after this long, the judge says. Victor would not move, and maybe he never could. Ruth walks out into the rain, and you walk out behind her.
endings.object: the open court doors in the rain
endings.picture: Tall double doors of a stone court building standing open onto wet steps and rain, warm light spilling out of the hall onto the steps, a small figure of Ruth with an umbrella on the right. Left half: grey stone and rain.

endings.label: HUNG JURY
endings.title: NO VERDICT
endings.text: Four hours, three votes, and the room never settles. The judge discharges you. There will be a retrial, a new twelve, the same recording. You hope one of them knows what an echo is.
endings.picture: An empty jury box in a wood-panelled courtroom after hours, twelve green leather seats, one reading lamp still on at the right end of the box. Left half: dark panelling and an empty public gallery.

endings.label: OUT OF CHANCES
endings.title: ELEVEN BECOME TWELVE
endings.text: Your arguments came out wrong and the room stopped listening. At five to six you raise your hand with the others. Gerald catches his train. You lie awake for a long time.
endings.picture: Twelve hands raised above the oak jury table, seen from low at the table's end, the nearest hand in a mustard cardigan sleeve, lit by the brass lamp on the right. Left half: dim ceiling and window.

scenes.title: ELEVEN TO ONE
scenes.object: the ballot slips under the lamp
scenes.picture: Gerald Pryce at the head of the oak table counting a small pile of folded paper slips under a brass lamp, on the right of the frame. Left half: the long empty end of the table and a rainy window.
scenes.story: Gerald Pryce, the foreman, counts the slips. "Eleven guilty. One not guilty." Every head turns towards you.
scenes.clue: Ruth was shouting at Simon the day before. You still have doubts.
scenes.prompt: Which sentence states your position correctly?
scenes.correct: Although she shouted, I'm not sure.
scenes.wrong1: Although she shouted, but I'm not sure.
scenes.wrong2: Despite she shouted, I'm not sure.
scenes.explanation: ALTHOUGH + a clause needs no BUT after it. DESPITE takes a noun or -ING, never a full clause like 'she shouted'.

scenes.title: THE CABBIE
scenes.picture: Danny Rourke leaning back in his chair on the right, arms wide, a steaming white mug of tea in front of him catching the lamp light. Left half: empty chairs and the panelled wall.
scenes.story: Danny Rourke drives a cab and has an opinion on everything. "She was angry. He's dead. Job done."
scenes.clue: You accept that she was angry. Anger alone proves nothing.
scenes.prompt: ___ her anger, it doesn't prove she pushed him.
scenes.explanation: A noun phrase follows the gap, so you need DESPITE. ALTHOUGH and EVEN THOUGH need a clause: 'although she was angry'.

scenes.title: THE HEADTEACHER
scenes.picture: Agnes Bell on the right, glasses on their chain, an open lined notebook and a yellow pencil in the lamp light in front of her, looking up. No writing visible on the page. Left half: the quiet table top.
scenes.story: Agnes Bell, a retired headteacher, has filled four pages in pencil. She looks up. "Go on, then. Convince me."
scenes.clue: Ruth lied to the police about when she left. You can't deny it.
scenes.prompt: Which sentence concedes the lie, then turns it?
scenes.correct: She lied. Even so, a lie isn't a push.
scenes.wrong1: She lied. Even though, a lie isn't a push.
scenes.wrong2: She lied. Despite, a lie isn't a push.
scenes.explanation: EVEN SO is an adverb that opens a new sentence. EVEN THOUGH and DESPITE are linkers and need something after them.

scenes.title: THE RECORDING PLAYS
scenes.picture: An open laptop on the oak table on the right, its screen glowing soft blue with a plain waveform shape and no writing, jurors' hands resting near it. Left half: dim table and window.
scenes.story: The usher brings in the laptop. Simon's phone recording plays again: shouting, a crash, then Ruth crying.
scenes.clue: You are a sound engineer. The crash is very hard to place.
scenes.prompt: ___ hard I listen, I can't tell what crashed.
scenes.explanation: HOWEVER + adjective or adverb + clause means 'it makes no difference how': however hard I listen. ALTHOUGH can't take 'hard' next.

scenes.title: THE NURSE
scenes.object: the photo of the bruised arm
scenes.picture: Priya Sandhu on the right holding up a large photograph of a man's forearm with a dark bruise, lit by the lamp; tasteful, no blood. Left half: the bare panelled wall.
scenes.story: Priya Sandhu works nights in A&E. "I've seen a hundred falls. That bruise on his arm worries me."
scenes.clue: The bruise worries her. The stair rail had been loose for months.
scenes.prompt: Which sentence answers Priya fairly?
scenes.correct: Worrying as it is, the rail was loose.
scenes.wrong1: Worrying as is it, the rail was loose.
scenes.wrong2: Worrying although it is, the rail was loose.
scenes.explanation: ADJECTIVE + AS + clause concedes a point: worrying as it is = although it is worrying. The subject comes before the verb.

scenes.title: THE FOREMAN'S TRAIN
scenes.picture: Close on Gerald Pryce's wrist on the right as he checks a steel wristwatch, navy blazer cuff, the lamp catching the watch face (no numbers needed). Left half: blurred rainy window.
scenes.story: Gerald checks his watch. "Look, I respect you. But it's eleven to one, and I've a train at six."
scenes.clue: You respect Gerald too. You still want the evidence looked at again.
scenes.prompt: ___ I respect you, we have to look again.
scenes.explanation: MUCH AS + clause is a formal ALTHOUGH, often with like or respect. DESPITE needs a noun; EVEN alone isn't a linker.

scenes.title: THE SHOUTING
scenes.picture: A pair of big studio headphones lying by the laptop on the right, a coiled cable, the lamp lighting them. Left half: the empty table top.
scenes.story: Headphones on. Ruth's voice: "You never finish anything!" Then Simon, laughing. Danny leans in. "Hear that? Furious."
scenes.clue: She sounds furious. Yet Simon is laughing, so he wasn't afraid.
scenes.prompt: She ___ furious, but Simon wasn't afraid of her.
scenes.explanation: MAY HAVE + past participle concedes a past possibility before BUT turns it. After a modal comes HAVE, never HAD or HAS.

scenes.title: THE CRASH
scenes.object: the mill kitchen in the flashback
scenes.picture: Flashback: the stone kitchen of a converted mill, a wooden chair knocked over and a broken jug on the flagstones on the right, lit by a pendant lamp; nobody in frame. Left half: a plain whitewashed wall.
scenes.story: You loop the crash five times. The echo is long: it happened far from the phone, near the kitchen.
scenes.clue: Ruth's voice is close to the phone at the very moment of the crash.
scenes.prompt: Which sentence makes your point correctly?
scenes.correct: Loud though it is, she's nowhere near it.
scenes.wrong1: Though loud it is, she's nowhere near it.
scenes.wrong2: Loud despite it is, she's nowhere near it.
scenes.explanation: ADJECTIVE + THOUGH + clause works like ADJECTIVE + AS: loud though it is. The adjective comes first, then THOUGH.

scenes.title: THE MISSING MINUTE
scenes.picture: Close on the laptop screen on the right: a soft glowing waveform with a clear flat gap in the middle, no numbers or writing, Mira's finger pointing at the gap. Left half: dark table.
scenes.story: The file is shorter than it should be. Fifty-eight seconds are missing between the crash and the crying.
scenes.clue: Nobody knows who cut it. It could have been Simon himself.
scenes.prompt: ___ the gap, the court accepted the recording.
scenes.explanation: IN SPITE OF + noun: in spite of the gap. Never IN SPITE without OF; EVEN THOUGH needs a subject and verb.

scenes.title: DANNY GOES QUIET
scenes.picture: Danny Rourke on the right wearing the big studio headphones, eyes closed, listening hard, the lamp on his face. Left half: empty chairs.
scenes.story: You play Danny the echo, then the gap. He is quiet for once. "All right. It's not as clear as I thought."
scenes.clue: Danny still thinks she's capable of it. But he admits there's doubt.
scenes.prompt: Danny: "___ she's capable of it, I can't be certain."
scenes.explanation: WHILE + clause can concede: while she's capable of it = although. WHEREAS compares two facts; NEVERTHELESS opens a new clause.

scenes.title: THE PHOTOGRAPHS
scenes.object: the photo of the broken rail
scenes.picture: Large police photographs spread on the table on the right, the top one showing iron spiral stairs and a gallery rail hanging from one bolt; no people, no writing. Left half: the plain table.
scenes.story: Priya spreads the police photos under the lamp. Iron stairs, a high gallery, a rail hanging from one bolt.
scenes.clue: The rail is broken. The prosecution says Ruth broke it in a struggle.
scenes.prompt: Which sentence answers the prosecution correctly?
scenes.correct: It's broken. That said, nobody knows when.
scenes.wrong1: It's broken. Although, nobody knows when.
scenes.wrong2: It's broken. That saying, nobody knows when.
scenes.explanation: THAT SAID at the start of a sentence concedes the point before it. ALTHOUGH can't stand alone before a comma.

scenes.title: THE BRUISE
scenes.picture: Priya Sandhu on the right gripping her own forearm with her other hand to show how a grip bruises, the lamp lighting her arm. Left half: the panelled wall.
scenes.story: Priya grips her own arm. "A hand makes a mark like that. So does a rail, if you grab it as you fall."
scenes.clue: You try every way to read the bruise as a grip. It still fits a fall.
scenes.prompt: ___ I might, I can't make it a push.
scenes.explanation: VERB + AS + subject + MIGHT concedes effort that failed: try as I might = although I try hard. Use the base verb.

scenes.title: THE EXPERIMENT
scenes.picture: Priya Sandhu standing on a jury chair on the right, one arm reaching out to an imaginary rail, mid-demonstration, lit by the lamp. Left half: tall empty window.
scenes.story: Priya stands on a chair, holds her arm out at gallery height, then lets it drop. "If he grabbed the rail... yes."
scenes.clue: Priya had doubts about a fall. Her experiment answers most of them.
scenes.prompt: Priya: "___ my doubts, a fall fits the injuries."
scenes.explanation: FOR ALL + noun = despite: for all my doubts. ALTHOUGH needs a clause, and IN SPITE needs OF.

scenes.title: THE RUSTED BOLT
scenes.object: the photo of the rusted bolt
scenes.picture: Close-up police photograph on the table on the right: a rusted iron bolt sheared through in an old wall bracket, lit by the lamp. No writing. Left half: dark table.
scenes.story: In the photo the bolt is rusted through. In March Simon emailed a builder about the rail. He never booked him.
scenes.clue: Ruth may or may not have been on the stairs. The rail was dangerous anyway.
scenes.prompt: Which sentence states the point correctly?
scenes.correct: Even if she was there, it was unsafe.
scenes.wrong1: Even though she was there, it was unsafe.
scenes.wrong2: Even she was there, it was unsafe.
scenes.explanation: EVEN IF: we don't know whether she was there. EVEN THOUGH would treat it as fact. EVEN alone isn't a linker.

scenes.title: ARTY TYPES
scenes.picture: Victor Lane on the right, arms on the table, a clear plastic sandwich box unopened in front of him under the lamp, his gold signet ring catching light. Left half: empty chairs.
scenes.story: Lunch arrives in plastic boxes. Victor Lane, a landlord, hasn't touched his. "Arty types. They all lie."
scenes.clue: Victor has judged her by her job, not the evidence. You keep calm.
scenes.prompt: ___ your feelings about artists, look at the facts.
scenes.explanation: WHATEVER + noun concedes any possibility: whatever your feelings = it makes no difference what they are. HOWEVER needs an adjective.

scenes.title: THE SECOND VOTE
scenes.picture: Victor Lane's heavy fist coming down on the oak table on the right, a small pile of paper slips jumping, lit by the lamp. Left half: blurred jurors in shadow.
scenes.story: Gerald calls a second vote. Nine guilty, three not guilty. Victor slams the table. "This is ridiculous."
scenes.clue: The vote has moved. Victor is just as certain as before.
scenes.prompt: Victor: "___ the vote, she's guilty."
scenes.explanation: REGARDLESS OF + noun = it makes no difference: regardless of the vote. The preposition is OF, never TO.

scenes.title: AT THE WINDOW
scenes.picture: Agnes Bell standing at a tall rain-streaked window on the right, a cup and saucer in her hands, the window lit warm from a lamp beside it. Left half: plain panelled wall.
scenes.story: You stand at the window with Agnes. Rain on the car park. "He's not a bad man," she says. "Just tired."
scenes.clue: Victor is rude. Agnes thinks he deserves a hearing anyway.
scenes.prompt: Agnes: "He's rude. ___, he deserves a hearing."
scenes.explanation: STILL at the start of a sentence concedes the last point: still, he deserves a hearing. ALTHOUGH and DESPITE must join to something.

scenes.title: KIT'S STATEMENT
scenes.picture: Flashback: Kit Marlow, nineteen, at a potter's wheel on the right in a clay-dusted mill workshop, big white headphones on, lit by a work lamp. Left half: plain shelves in shadow.
scenes.story: Kit Marlow, the apprentice, told the court he heard "a scream, then a thud" from the stairwell at half past two.
scenes.clue: Kit sounded honest. He was also wearing headphones at the wheel.
scenes.prompt: Which sentence is fair to Kit?
scenes.correct: He may be honest, but he had headphones on.
scenes.wrong1: He may honest, but he had headphones on.
scenes.wrong2: He may is honest, but he had headphones on.
scenes.explanation: MAY + base verb ... BUT concedes, then turns: he may be honest, but. MAY never takes IS, and BE can't be dropped.

scenes.title: EXHIBIT FOURTEEN
scenes.picture: A pair of white noise-cancelling headphones in a clear evidence bag on the oak table on the right, lit by the lamp; the bag has no label or writing. Left half: dark table top.
scenes.story: Exhibit 14: Kit's headphones, found on the wheel. You know this model. It blocks out almost everything.
scenes.clue: Kit's music was loud. A scream might still get through, just about.
scenes.prompt: ___ loud the music was, a scream might get through.
scenes.explanation: NO MATTER HOW + adjective + clause: no matter how loud the music was. Loud is an adjective, so there's no MUCH.

scenes.title: GERALD LISTENS
scenes.picture: Gerald Pryce on the right in the white headphones, back turned to Agnes who is mid-shout behind him in soft focus, the lamp on Gerald's face. Left half: empty wall.
scenes.story: Gerald puts on the headphones himself and plays music. Agnes screams behind him. Gerald doesn't turn round.
scenes.clue: Gerald heard almost nothing. He wanted to go home. Now he wants it right.
scenes.prompt: Gerald: "___ to go home, I'm changing my vote."
scenes.explanation: DESPITE + -ING: despite wanting to go home. Never DESPITE + subject and verb, and never DESPITE OF.

scenes.title: THE WHITE VAN
scenes.object: the white van in the lane
scenes.picture: Flashback, wide-angle doorbell-camera view: a white van pulling out of a stone mill yard into a wet lane on the right, its headlights on. No numbers, no timestamp, no writing. Left half: an empty grey lane.
scenes.story: A neighbour's doorbell camera shows Ruth's van leaving the mill at 14:25. Her 999 call comes at 14:52.
scenes.clue: Simon died between two and three, so the times don't clear her.
scenes.prompt: Which sentence concedes the point correctly?
scenes.correct: It isn't proof. And yet it matters.
scenes.wrong1: It isn't proof. Although it matters.
scenes.wrong2: It isn't proof. Despite it matters.
scenes.explanation: AND YET can open a new sentence. 'Although it matters' has no main clause, and DESPITE can't take a subject and verb.

scenes.title: TWELVE MINUTES
scenes.picture: Flashback: a rainy builders' and clay merchant's yard, stacked sacks under a lit canopy on the right, the white van parked beside them. No signs or writing. Left half: open wet yard.
scenes.story: The van's satnav was read out in court: twelve minutes to the clay merchant, twelve back, one stop on the way.
scenes.clue: She could have driven fast. The satnav says she kept to the limit.
scenes.prompt: ___ she could have driven fast, the satnav says not.
scenes.explanation: THOUGH + clause = although: though she could have driven fast. EVEN alone isn't a linker; IN SPITE OF needs a noun.

scenes.title: IT DOESN'T ADD UP
scenes.picture: Gerald Pryce on the right, his steel wristwatch taken off and laid on the oak table in the lamp light, Gerald staring at it, chin on hand. Left half: dim window.
scenes.story: Gerald takes off his watch and lays it on the table. "Twelve there, twelve back, and a stop. It doesn't add up."
scenes.clue: Gerald's train matters to him. The timeline matters more now.
scenes.prompt: Gerald: "___ my train, I'll stay until we're sure."
scenes.explanation: IN SPITE OF + noun: in spite of my train. IN SPITE needs OF; EVEN THOUGH needs a subject and verb.

scenes.title: ELEVEN TO ONE AGAIN
scenes.picture: Victor Lane on the right, alone at his end of the table, looking down at his own clasped hands with the gold signet ring, lit by the lamp. Left half: empty chairs pushed back.
scenes.story: It's eleven to one again, the other way. Victor looks at his hands. "My son walked out too. Never said why."
scenes.clue: Victor is hurting. You understand him, and you still need his vote.
scenes.prompt: ___ I understand, this isn't about your son.
scenes.explanation: AS MUCH AS + clause concedes a feeling: as much as I understand. Both ASes are needed; SO MUCH AS means something else.

scenes.title: THE LAST BALLOT
scenes.object: the last slip in Victor's hand
scenes.picture: Victor Lane's hand on the right placing a folded paper slip onto a small pile in front of Gerald, lit by the lamp. Left half: the dark panelled door with a thin line of light under it.
scenes.story: The usher knocks. Gerald holds out his hand for the slips. Victor's is the last to go onto the pile.
scenes.clue: You'll never know what happened on those stairs. The doubt is reasonable.
scenes.prompt: Which sentence closes the case correctly?
scenes.correct: Although we can't know, we must decide.
scenes.wrong1: Although we can't know, but we must decide.
scenes.wrong2: Despite we can't know, we must decide.
scenes.explanation: ALTHOUGH + clause, then the main clause, with no BUT. DESPITE can't take 'we can't know': it needs a noun or -ING.
